lines.text: Today we look at how games fake gravity.
Velocity is defined as how far something moves each frame.
Gravity is just a number added to the vertical velocity every frame.
For example, if gravity is half a pixel, a falling player speeds up smoothly.
Remember to cap the falling speed, or players will pass through thin floors.
In other words, terminal velocity keeps collisions reliable.
Finally, many games lower gravity at the top of a jump so it feels floaty and fair.

summary: Gravity in games is a number added to vertical velocity each frame.
Cap the falling speed so collisions stay reliable.
Lower gravity at the top of a jump feels fair.
